title: Food and drink

fn.en: Talk about food and say what there is and isn’t in your kitchen.

useful: Could I have a kilo of…?

items.q: You boil water in a ___ to make tea.
You fry eggs and mushrooms in a ___ pan.
To roast meat you need a very hot ___.
You need a sharp ___ to chop the onions.
Mix the water and flour in a ___ with a spoon.
Two minutes and the food is hot: the ___.

lines: Do you have [any|some|a] beef? — Yes, we have [some|any|a] nice steaks. 🥩
Could I have [a|some|any] kilo of beef cubes, please? 🔢
Do you have [any|some|a] yoghurt? — No, I’m afraid we [don’t|aren’t|haven’t]. 🥛
We have [some|any|a] bags of rice, but there isn’t [any|some|a] pasta today. 🍚
There [are|is|aren’t] some mushrooms in the fridge, but there [isn’t|aren’t|is] any bread. 🍄

sub.en: Look at the sentences. When do you use some, and when any?

items.why: some in positive sentences; any in negatives and questions.

items.q: I’m afraid we don’t have ___ rice.

items.why: One thing you can count takes a / an, not some.

items.q: There ___ some mushrooms in the fridge.

items.why: bread is uncountable, so it takes is — even with any.

items.q: Can I have ___ of beef, please?

items.a: Could I have a kilo of beef please

items.from: There is a lemon in the fridge.
items.a: There are three lemons in the fridge

use: Could I have a kilo of…?
tts: Hello. Can I help you? — Hi. Yes, please. Do you have any beef?
Yes, we have some nice steaks here. We also have some small beef cubes.
OK. Can I have some beef cubes? About a kilo, please. And I’d also like a small steak. — Just one? — Yes, just one. Thanks.
Also, do you have any yoghurt? — No, I’m afraid we don’t. — What about rice? Do you have any rice? — Yes, we have some bags of rice.

items.s: The customer wants about a kilo of beef cubes.

tts: What do I have in my kitchen? Not much, really. I have a kettle, because I make a lot of tea. And I have one frying pan and two saucepans. I don’t really need anything else. Oh — I forgot the most important thing in my kitchen: the microwave!
There’s nothing special about my kitchen. I have all the usual things. But I have a beautiful old set of plates and bowls for when people come for dinner.

items.q: The second speaker has something special:

acts.title: What’s in the fridge
text: Aigul opens the fridge on Sunday evening and writes a list.
“There’s some yoghurt, but there isn’t any milk. There are three lemons and a lot of olives, because I always buy too many. There isn’t any bread and there aren’t any mushrooms.”
“There’s some rice in the cupboard and there’s half a packet of pasta. There’s a kilo of beef in the freezer, but it’s frozen, so it isn’t dinner tonight.”

items.s: There is some yoghurt in the fridge.
There is some rice in the cupboard.
She is going to cook the beef tonight.

use: Could I have a kilo of…?

items.sit: You are at the butcher’s and you want to know if they sell beef.
You want one kilo of beef cubes.
o: Could I have a kilo of beef cubes, please?
Could I have a kilos of beef cubes, please?
Could I have some kilo of beef cubes?

items.sit: You are the shop assistant. You have no yoghurt today.
o: I’m afraid we don’t have any.
I’m afraid we don’t have some.
I’m afraid we aren’t have any.

items.sit: A friend asks about bread at your house. There is none.
You have five or six mushrooms in the fridge.
You ask a shop assistant for one lemon.
o: Could I have a lemon, please?
Could I have some lemon, please?
Could I have any lemon, please?

And rice? Is there ___ rice left? 🍚

write.q: Open your fridge and your cupboard. Write 6 sentences: three things there are and three things there aren’t. Watch is / are and some / any.
write.model: There’s some yoghurt and there’s a lot of rice in the cupboard. There are four lemons and there are some olives. There isn’t any bread and there isn’t any honey. There aren’t any mushrooms, so I can’t make the soup. There’s a kilo of beef in the freezer for Sunday.

speak.q: Play both parts in a shop out loud: ask for two things with “Do you have any…?”, ask for a quantity, and refuse one thing politely as the assistant.
speak.model: Do you have any beef? — Yes, we have some nice steaks. Could I have a kilo, please? Do you have any yoghurt? — No, I’m afraid we don’t.
